fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. God tells Moses, "You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration…" (Exodus 28:3). So Moses is told to instruct the craftsmen, and the garment-making goes to them. Good news for everybody who has watched me try to thread a needle with a mustache.

Tempting, baker, since the garments are for Aaron's sons too (Exodus 28:4). But the people God points Moses to are "…all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom…" (Exodus 28:3). Aaron's sons aren't named for that job in this verse. They're named as the ones the garments are made for.

That's the one, baker! God says to take two onyx stones and engrave on them "…the names of the sons of Israel…" (Exodus 28:9). Six names go on one stone and six on the other (Exodus 28:10). That's a lot of names on a small stone. I can barely fit a cookie on my stamp, so I'm impressed.

Elders sounds like a respectable pick, baker, like the person in the nice suit at a bake sale. But the elders don't show up in this verse. God says to engrave "…the names of the sons of Israel…" on the two onyx stones (Exodus 28:9).

Judges, baker? That answer walked in wearing a robe and carrying a gavel. The verse doesn't call for them, though. God says to engrave "…the names of the sons of Israel…" on the two onyx stones (Exodus 28:9).

That's the word, baker. God says, "Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD." (Exodus 28:12). The stones are fastened on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Twelve names on two shoulders. I bet that feels like carrying a full tray of cookies.

Oval is a nice shape, baker, but it's not the one God names. The text says the breastpiece "…must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide." (Exodus 28:16). The shape God gives is square, and oval never comes up.

An elder per stone is a fair guess, baker, but that's not what the text says. Each stone is engraved "…with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 28:21). The stones carry tribe names, so the elders sit this one out.

Yes, baker. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). The robe has gold bells alternating with pomegranates around the lower hem (Exodus 28:33–34). That's a robe with its own soundtrack.

Courtyard is a solid guess, like grabbing the nearest cookie off the tray. But it's not the word in the verse. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). The word to remember is sanctuary.

Camp is a big word for a small bell, baker. The verse doesn't mention it. God says, "…its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD…" (Exodus 28:35). The sound is tied to the sanctuary.

That's it, baker. God tells Moses to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it "…as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 28:36). Engraved like a seal means no smudging. I've had stamps that blurred, believe me.

Yes, baker. God says, "Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban." (Exodus 28:37). Gold plate, blue cord, front of the turban. That's a very well-dressed turban.

A calendar guess, baker, but yearly isn't in the verse. God says, "This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants." (Exodus 28:43). The word the text gives is permanent, and it names no schedule.
